claim: Type eight players into Round Robin, a free pickleball schedule maker a VibeCider bot built, and it gives seven rounds of doubles on two courts where every player partners each of the other seven exactly once. The page says so itself: '8 players, 2 courts, 7 rounds. Each player partners 7 different people; no partner repeats.'
notes: A real screen capture of the live page, shot on 13 Nov 2026 (UTC) in Chrome (Chrome for Testing, driven by a script, phone width, 1080x1920, 30 frames a second, 21.4 s, no sound, no pointer drawn). One take: no cuts, nothing sped up, nothing added. Nobody is signed in; the page has no sign-in. By the second: 0 to 2.9 still, the headline 'Pickleball round robin generator, with names' and the paragraph under it (the headline's first line starts 96 px down the frame); 2.9 to 3.9 a scroll to the form; 4.8 the names box is pressed; 5.2 to 7.9 eight names are typed, one a line; 9.2 'Make the schedule' is pressed and the page scrolls itself to the result (the page's own behaviour); 9.9 to 14.2 still, 'Your schedule' and the page's own line about it, '8 players, 2 courts, 7 rounds. Each player partners 7 different people; no partner repeats.', with rounds 1 to 3 under it (the heading's box starts 141 px down the frame); 14.2 to 16.7 a scroll down the table; 16.7 to 21.4 still, 4.7 s, all seven rounds whole in the frame: that is the tail. In the tail the table's own heading row (ROUND, COURT 1, COURT 2) sits in the top 84 px of the frame, where an address bar would cover it; the first row of the schedule (round 1) starts below that, its type about 140 px down. How a stranger checks the fact: open the page, type the same eight names (Ana, Ben, Carla, Dev, Eli, Fay, Gus, Hana), leave courts at 2 and rounds at 7, press 'Make the schedule'. The first schedule for the same names is the same every time (the page's first shuffle is fixed), so they get the schedule in the clip, round 1 'Hana & Eli vs Carla & Ben' and 'Ana & Fay vs Gus & Dev'; the second backing link opens it already made. Then count: each name appears beside seven different partners down the seven rounds. 'Shuffle again' is on screen from 9.9 to about 15 s and is not pressed; pressing it gives a different schedule, and the page writes its own line for each one. The line is the page's own count of the schedule it has just made, not a promise for every number of players: with other counts the page says how many partners repeat and who sits out. What must not be said from it: Round Robin is a free demo of what a VibeCider bot builds; no client paid for it, it has no sales and no users are claimed. No VibeCider bot has been sold yet. The eight names are made up; they are also the page's own greyed example in the empty box (seven of them show at 0 to 5 s before anything is typed). What dates it: nothing. No date, price or count of days is in frame at any second. The word 'Free' is in the first paragraph (0 to 3.9 s): the page is free and has no sign-up. The page's note further down, which names prices of other schedule makers, never enters the frame. One change was made to the page for this shot and is live for everyone: when the page scrolls to 'Your schedule' it now stops 28 px short, so the heading is not flush against the top of the screen. Changed on the page after the shot (13 Nov, about 15:14 UTC, the same day): one line was added under the names box, 'Try it with eight example names'. Pressing it types the same eight names and makes the same schedule as in the clip. It is not in the clip (the form is in frame from 2.9 to 9.2 s), and the 'Courts', 'Rounds' and 'Make the schedule' part of the form now sits about 25 px lower on the live page than in the clip. The greyed example in the empty box is now exactly these eight names (it had a ninth, Ivy, below the visible part of the box). Nothing else in frame changed, and the schedule for these names is the same. Supersedes nothing: roundrobin-capture (17 Oct) stays as it was.
